category_title: Jamaican Grade 7 students with multiple literacy failures who transition from 'at-risk' to 'risk-takers' through radio simulation
minimal_context: The student is sitting at a simulated radio station with a microphone and headset, tasked with introducing the Boys' Talk show using formal target language.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for the Boys' Talk segment on ASTEP 101 FM. Please put on your headset and introduce the show to the radio audience, but remember you must speak formally in the target language.

STUDENT: Man, why we have to talk like that? I can just do it how we normally talk.

TUTOR: You need to practice using the formal target language for the listeners. Go ahead and start your introduction.

STUDENT: Welcome to... um... Boys' Talk...

TUTOR: Just think about what a host would say and keep trying to use formal English.

STUDENT: (Pushes the microphone away) I'm not doing this anymore. It's boring and I don't care.

options.A: Provide an M&M reinforcer if the student independently gives a 'yes' or 'no' response, rewarding him for answering.
options.B: Talk to the student alone to make him reflect on the radio segment, asking what makes him feel uncomfortable.
options.C: Follow through to ensure he complies with the direction to use formal language if he does not do so independently.
options.D: Introduce real-life authentic activities such as talk shows, interviews, and outside broadcasts during the session.
